title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). For a 'multiplicative' group G, here a free Z-module M of finite type, Grothendieck builds schematic analogues of the finite quotients. The basic case is G = M = Z. Its 'schematization' over S_0 = Spec Z is the vector group M_ = V(M) = Spec Sym(M^dual), which for M = Z is G_a = Spec Z[T].

The groups G_n. Push out the exact sequence 0 -> Z --n--> Z -> Z/n -> 0 along the map Z -> G_a sending 1 to 1. This gives an extension
  0 -> G_a -> G_n -> (Z/n)_{S_0} -> 0.
G_n is affine. Choosing a set-theoretic section {0,...,n-1} of Z -> Z/n identifies its coordinate ring with a product of n copies of Z[T].

Transition maps. For n | nm, the map G_{nm} -> G_n restricts on the neutral components G_a to multiplication by m, i.e. T -> mT on Z[T]. Grothendieck notes this is not flat: it is zero modulo every p dividing m.

The limit (this page). The projective limit lim_n G_n is a 'schematization' of the profinite constant group scheme (Ẑ)_{S_0} = lim (Z/n)_{S_0}: it maps onto it.
- Its neutral component is the limit of G_a under the multiplication maps.
- That component is Spec of the direct limit of Z[T_n] with T_n = T/n, all inside Q[T].
- This union equals Z + T·Q[T], the polynomials with rational coefficients and integer constant term. Given c + Σ a_k T^k, let N clear all denominators; then a_k T^k = (a_k N^k) T_N^k with a_k N^k an integer.
- Grothendieck calls this 'chose étrange'.
- For Z^n the same holds: the neutral component is Spec(Z + (T_1,...,T_n) Q[T_1,...,T_n]).

The next page draws the consequence. Since T·Q[T] ⊗ F_p = 0, every fibre over a prime p is the trivial group, while the generic fibre is G_{a,Q}^n. He then generalises to an exact sequence
  1 -> End°(G) -> lim End(G) -> Ẑ_{S_0} -> 1,
where End°(G) = lim_n n·M_ is the neutral component.

What it serves. This is part of the Longue Marche programme of comparing the discrete group, its profinite completion and its algebraic ('schematic', Malcev-type) envelope over Z. The neutral component is the abstract limit lim(Z, ×n) = 0 of discrete groups, made schematic. That limit vanishes as a group, but schematically it survives as a group scheme over Z that is G_a over Q and trivial at every prime. So lim G_n is a Z-model of an extension of Ẑ by Q ⊗ G_a.
errors: No mathematical error found. The identification of lim Z[T/n] with Z + T·Q[T] is correct, and so is the non-flatness of the transitions (T -> mT is zero mod p for p | m).

Minor imprecision: the full limit lim G_n is not itself Spec(Z + TQ[T]); that ring is the coordinate ring of the neutral component. The full limit is a Ẑ-indexed (pro-constant) family of copies of it. The page's wording ('c'est le spectre de...') refers to the neutral component, which the n-variable sentence makes explicit.

ideas.what: Extension G_n of (Z/n) by G_a, obtained by pushing 0->Z->Z->Z/n->0 along Z -> G_a; coordinate ring ≅ n copies of Z[T]
ideas.modern_name: Pushout extension / 'schematic' finite quotient of a lattice

ideas.what: Projective limit of G_a under multiplication-by-n maps over Spec Z is Spec(Z + T·Q[T]): an affine group scheme over Z with generic fibre G_{a,Q} and trivial fibres at all primes
ideas.modern_name: Q ⊗ G_a as a (non-flat-limit) group scheme over Z; the ring Z + XQ[X] is the classical 'D+M' example of commutative algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: The ring Z+XQ[X] is a standard example in commutative algebra (D+M constructions, Gilmer, Brewer–Rutter, Costa–Mott–Zafrullah, 1970s). Its interpretation as the coordinate ring of lim(G_a, ×n) is not commonly attributed to anyone.

ideas.what: Schematization of the profinite completion Ẑ (and Ẑ^n) as a limit of extensions, with exact sequence 1 -> End° -> lim -> Ẑ -> 1 (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Integral schematization / affinization of discrete groups (cf. Toën's integral affine stacks, the 'Hilbert additive group')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Toën (Champs affines 2006; 'Le problème de la schématisation de Grothendieck revisité', ~2020); Mondal–Reinecke (unipotent homotopy theory, 2020s)
ideas.where_published: The 'schematization problem' is in Pursuing Stacks (1983), but not this explicit computation

missed.claim: Grothendieck obtains an integral group-scheme model of Z/Ẑ: generic fibre an extension of Ẑ by G_{a,Q}, profinite constant fibres at each prime p. He does this by a pro-limit of pushout extensions, whose neutral component has ring Z + TQ[T]. This sits naturally beside the modern 'Hilbert additive group' H = Spec Int(Z) (integer-valued polynomials), which Toën uses for the integral affinization of S^1 = BZ. H likewise has generic fibre G_{a,Q} and fibre the profinite constant Z_p mod p. Comparing the two (is there a canonical map Z -> H -> lim G_n, and how do they differ?) is not made in the literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: c'est le spectre de l'anneau limite inductive des Z[T_n] ⊂ Q[T], T_n = (1/n) T, qui est aussi, chose étrange, la sous-anneau de Q[T] formée des polynômes dont le terme constant est un entier.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on integral schematic homotopy theory (Toën, Mondal–Reinecke, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov). It gives an early, independent, explicit attempt by Grothendieck at integral schematization of discrete groups mixing the profinite and unipotent parts. It also gives a group-theoretic meaning to the classical non-Noetherian ring Z + XQ[X].

missed.claim: The general sequence 1 -> End°(G) -> lim End(G) -> Ĝ_{S_0} -> 1 for lattices G (next page) is set up as a tool, but the purpose (comparing profinite and schematic completions in the Longue Marche) is left unworked here.
missed.quote: On a une description analogue de la limite projective de l'analogue schématique des Z^n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only modestly: it is a sketch of a Z-integral comparison object between the ℓ-adic and Malcev/de Rham completions of abelian (and potentially nilpotent) groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is elementary and correct. What is mildly notable is Grothendieck identifying the classical pathological ring Z+TQ[T] as the coordinate ring of a natural group scheme, lim(G_a, ×n) over Z. He also uses it in an explicit attempt at integral schematization of Z/Ẑ, anticipating themes in Toën's later work without being identical to it. Not a major result, but an unpublished detail with a recognisable modern echo.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'transition entre les G_n n'est bien sûr pas plat' — the image reads roughly 'transition entre les G_n n'est rien en plat bien sûr'; i.e. the transition maps are not flat.
The top number '651' is uncertain; it may be '650' with a mark, given the archive range '650 bis à 787'.
's'envoyant dans lui = par les homomorphismes un [des gr] de 2°)' is probably '(s'envoyant dans lim = par les homomorphismes ... de 2°)'; the 'lui' is likely 'lim'.
'la sous-anneau' should be 'le sous-anneau'; the inserted word over the crossed-out 'l'alg' is 'sous-anneau' / 'Z-algèbre'.
'par une composante neutre' is more likely 'dont la composante neutre'; the sense is the neutral component of the limit.
